subject: MedRex Private Deploy: BYO-K & HSM network / rotation constraints
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@medrex.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: paul.klein@medrex.com, ds-team@medrex.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: MedRex private deploy — BYO-K and HSM network constraints

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving toward a private VPC deployment in our AWS account and need to lock down the BYO-K and HSM constraints so we can finish our internal security review. Top questions from the Security and Infra teams:

- Physical topology: can HSM appliance be co-located in our on-prem colocation or must it be a managed cloud HSM?
- Network ports & egress: which host->HSM and Redwood-controlplane flows need to be opened?
- Key rotation: can we support 1) customer-controlled BYOK rotation cadence (monthly/quart) and 2) emergency key zeroize from our on-call?
- Evidence: what artifacts (attestation PDFs, CSR hashes, audit log snapshots) will Redwood provide during provisioning and for SOC2 evidence?

We have a hard compliance gate: netflow must show no unencrypted egress to external networks outside our control and operator roles must be separable from Redwood support.

I've attached a sketch of our intended VPC/subnet layout. Can you reply with a short design that addresses the bullet items above and a list of next steps?

Regards,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Security Ops, MedRex Health
Attachments: medrex-byo-topology-sketch.png (referenced)
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: alice.zhang@medrex.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: paul.klein@medrex.com, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedRex private deploy — BYO-K and HSM network constraints

Hi Alice — thanks, this is helpful. High-level answers up front then a proposed set of actions. I'll keep this concise so you can paste into the review doc.

1) Topology options
- On-prem HSM in your colo: supported. Redwood Private supports a hybrid keybacked model where the HSM (FIPS 140-2/3 certified) is customer-attested and sits on your network. We integrate over an IPSEC tunnel or private cross-connect and never persist unwrapped key material.
- Cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Key Vault HSM): supported as well if you prefer managed cloud appliances. Either mode is compatible with BYOK.

2) Network flows (minimum required)
- Controlplane (Redwood -> your controlplane endpoint): TLS 443 outbound, expected to be allowed for management only. We recommend tagging and limiting to specific management instances/subnets.
- HSM interconnect: 10.0.X.Y/TCP 1792 (example vendor port) or vendor-specific ports — we'll provide a CSV of vendor ports for the chosen appliance. Traffic is mutual-TLS and restricted to the HSM appliance IPs.
- No plaintext token egress: all tokens/keys remain wrapped with your KEK; model inference traffic does not carry unwrapped KEKs.

3) Rotation and emergency zeroize
- Rotation cadence: yes — we support customer-triggered key rotation via API (you retain KMS privileges to generate, wrap, and promote new KEKs). Rotation windows can be automated (cron) or manual.
- Emergency zeroize: we expose a guaranteed zeroize hook that can be invoked by your custodians. For private on-prem HSM that must be exercised locally; we provide a signed acknowledgement and an audit entry to Redwood Console.

4) Evidence and artifacts
- Attestation bundles (MFG attestation chain), signed CSR fingerprints, and audit log snapshots (JSON) for provisioning.
- We can provide a timebound export to S3 (or an in-account bucket) for you to ingest into your evidence locker.

Next steps (proposed):
- Redwood: share vendor-ports.csv + medrex-specific network diagram template (attached).
- MedRex: confirm HSM mode (on-prem vs cloud) and list operator principals who will hold custodial rights.
- Joint: schedule a short network preflight call to validate peering and flow rules.

I've attached a small example of the vendor ports we typically require (hsm-network-ports.csv) and a sample rotation policy draft. Marissa: can you add any runbook/ops notes?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: hsm-network-ports.csv, rotation-policy-draft.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, alice.zhang@medrex.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedRex private deploy — BYO-K and HSM network constraints

Hi team — quick ops notes to add to Hannah's excellent summary:

- Rotation automation: suggest a canary promote window (24–72h) where new KEK is pushed to a small set of inference nodes and telemetry is validated before global cutover. We can provide an example canary policy for your change control.
- Audit evidence: we will provide per-rotation audit lines showing key-id, rotated_by (principal), method (api/scheduled), and pre/post-hash fingerprints. These map directly to SOC2 evidence items.
- Operator separation: strongly recommend at least 3 custodians in a split-witness model for HSM ceremonies. If MedRex requires hardware tokens or smartcards for custodian auth, we can support that as a requirement.

Small caveat: on-prem HSM zeroize requires physical or VPN-restricted access unless you provide a remote-triggered KMS agent behind your firewall; discuss during preflight.

Marissa Cole
Director, Applied Security
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: alice.zhang@medrex.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, paul.klein@medrex.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedRex private deploy — BYO-K and HSM network constraints

Alice / Paul — operational clarifications from infra/security ops perspective:

- Network hardening: please ensure HSM VLAN is isolated with ACLs and that the cross-connect only allows Redwood management IPs and your operator host IPs. We recommend private peering over a dedicated interface rather than shared transit.
- Egress restrictions: Redwood will default to no external outbound to third-party telemetry endpoints from the private deployment. If you require Redwood support access (for troubleshooting), we'll do a time-limited bastion-access model with explicit ACL exemptions and recorded session playback.
- Compliance evidence: attachable artifacts we can deliver to Procurement: vendor attestation PDF, list of personnel with custodian roles, rotation logs (CSV), and a signed DPA addendum for key custody.

Attachment: I've added a short checklist (medrex-byo-kickoff-diagram.pdf) with suggested subnet and ACL entries. Please confirm whether your compliance team requires an on-site HSM audit before go-live — we can coordinate vendor availability (VendorSecure).

-Kimberly Park
VP, Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: paul.klein@medrex.com <paul.klein@medrex.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, alice.zhang@medrex.com
Cc: procurement@medrex.com, ds-team@medrex.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedRex private deploy — BYO-K and HSM network constraints

Thanks everyone — this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers from MedRex:

- We'll proceed with on-prem HSM in our colo and require an on-site audit prior to activation.
- Operator principals: paul.klein@medrex.com, alice.zhang@medrex.com, and ds-lead@medrex.com will serve as initial custodians. We'll provide smartcard tokens for the ceremony.
- Next steps: procurement will take the DPA and attestation docs; please send vendor availability for a week window (we prefer 2027-05-24 to 2027-05-28).

Paul Klein
Sr. Infra Manager, MedRex Health
